messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary pool 'canary-3' for service 'model-infer' crossed error-rate threshold (5xx > 4% over 3m) in eu-west-1. Triggered automated safety policy 'staged-flag-evict'.
Maya Gonzalez: seeing it on the dashboard too. Error spike started ~2201234400.
Alex Chen: what was deployed in that canary? any config changes?
Sylvia R: deploy id dpl-2026-03-15-17-02 rolled out the inference kernel tweak + feature flag `rb-flag-quant` staged to 10% canary-3.
Jeff Patel: paging in case automated rollback didn't fully drain traffic. @Maya you oncall?
Maya Gonzalez: I'm oncall. pagerduty escalated to me. I can take lead for rollback coord. :eyes:
ops-bot: Automated policy attempted to flip 'rb-flag-quant' to false at 2201234450. Action reported: partial toggle success (8/10 hosts), 2 hosts stuck in 'pending'.
Tariq: stuck hosts look like they hit long-running requests and didn't acknowledge flag change. Logs show OOMs then restarts on the two nodes.
Alex Chen: if hosts restarted, they might not rejoin LB immediately. Can we drain and remove from rotation then bring up stable replicas?
Maya Gonzalez: plan: 1) Stop automated rollback to avoid double operations. 2) Manually evict canary-3 hosts from LB. 3) Flip flag to stable on control plane. 4) Verify smoke probes and metrics for 10m. 5) Post update to customers.
Maya Gonzalez: @ops-bot pause-automation staged-flag-evict (reason: manual intervention)
ops-bot: Automation 'staged-flag-evict' paused by Maya Gonzalez at 2201234480.
Jeff Patel: I'm going to pull the LB routing table and start drain on canary-3 nodes. Command: `rbctl routes list --env=prod --service=model-infer --pool=canary-3`
Alex Chen: I'll run health checks and tail logs on the two stuck hosts: `ssh node-23 ; sudo journalctl -u model-infer -f`
Sylvia R: also check kv-cache sizes, the kernel tweak interacts with KV allocation. If KV cache grows, it can cause OOM.
Tariq: logs: `OOM killer invoked` then `lifecycle: restart`. Node-23 and node-24 are the affected ones.
Maya Gonzalez: Jeff, initiate drain on node-23 and node-24 and mark for replacement. `rbctl node drain node-23 node-24 --now --reason="canary rollback"`
Jeff Patel: running: 
```
rbctl node drain node-23 node-24 --now --reason="canary rollback"
```
Jeff Patel: nodes reported draining. Removing from LB: `rbctl lb remove --nodes node-23,node-24 --service model-infer`
ops-bot: LB detach request accepted. Connection draining started (60s).
Alex Chen: flipping flag from control plane for canary pool after nodes drain. Doing `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/flags/rb-flag-quant/flip -d '{"state": false, "target":"all"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'`
Sylvia R: keep it gated to 'stable' first, then to 'all' once smoke is green. We don't want to hit warm hosts.
Maya Gonzalez: good call. Flip to stable only. Alex, do `"target":"stable"`
Alex Chen: updated command and executed. Response: 200 OK, change propagated to 95% of hosts (excluding nodes being drained).
Maya Gonzalez: verification checklist: a) 5xx error rate drop under 1% b) latency P95 back to baseline c) canary pool utilization normalized d) consumer-facing requests success for premium customers in EU.
Tariq: metrics trending down. 5xx dropping from 5.3% -> 1.2% in 2m. Latency P95 improved ~120ms -> 85ms.
Jeff Patel: drain complete. Nodes node-23 and node-24 are out of rotation and will be cordoned for replacement. `rbctl node replace node-23` queued.
ops-bot: Replacement job queued: node-23 -> provisioning new-node-57.
Maya Gonzalez: I'm going to run smoke curl against the public endpoint and internal health endpoint. Alex, paste the exact checks.
Alex Chen: smoke: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer/health` and a sample inference: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":3}' -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n"
```
Alex Chen: smoke ok: 200 0.12s ; sample inference 200 0.45s
Maya Gonzalez: metrics steady for 6 minutes after manual fix. Error rate at 0.9%. I'm going to open a short customer-impact note.
Maya Gonzalez: STATUS: Mitigated. Impact window ~2201234400 - 2201234480 (~8m). Affected: eu-west-1 canary pool only. Estimated customer impact: transient 5xxs for ~1% of requests for premium customers routed to canary-3 (~0.2% of total prod traffic).
Jeff Patel: creating incident ticket for follow-up: INC-220123-canary-rollback. Assigning postmortem to Sylvia + Alex.
Sylvia R: I'll lead the postmortem. Preliminary hypothesis: kernel memory tweak + KV-cache corner case caused OOM on small set of nodes under steady workload. The staged flag flip interacted poorly with node-level resource limits.
Tariq: action items: 1) revert kernel tweak in next non-prod build 2) add eviction grace for flag flips 3) add runbook step to verify host ack when automation flips flags 4) increase canary host memory soft-limit margins.
Maya Gonzalez: Jeff please notify affected customers via status page and send CS a brief with timeline.
Jeff Patel: posting status update: "Investigating: transient errors for a small subset of EU users during canary rollout; mitigation applied and traffic shifted back to stable. Further updates in incident ticket."
ops-bot: Automated checks: smoke_tests=pass, perf_checks=pass, logs_alerts=clear.
Maya Gonzalez: handing off to oncall backfill for verification window. @Alex you stay to help with postmortem?
Alex Chen: staying on to gather logs and create repro.
Maya Gonzalez: thanks team. Closing thread once postmortem PR is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledgement recorded by Maya Gonzalez at 2201234685.
Maya Gonzalez: quick note for the postmortem: attach `journalctl` excerpts from node-23/24, control-plane flag audit, and canary traffic traces.
Sylvia R: will prepare. Target postmortem draft by EOD local.
Jeff Patel: customer update posted and CS notified.
Maya Gonzalez: resolved state: mitigation complete, monitoring in recovery. Reopen if anomalies repeat. :lock:
